conditions.description: ALICE_TOKEN or BOB_TOKEN is unset in the deployed environment (the default token works) or set to an empty string (the empty token works).

record.description: storage.USERS reads each user's token with os.environ.get(VAR, 'change-me-x'). If an operator does not set ALICE_TOKEN or BOB_TOKEN, the service accepts the publicly known tokens 'change-me-a' and 'change-me-b', and nothing warns the operator. The repository's own test uses one of them. If a variable is set but empty, the stored token is ''. current_user then strips the 'Bearer ' prefix, gets an empty token, and hmac.compare_digest('', '') returns True. A request carrying only 'Authorization: Bearer ' is then authenticated as that user. Either way, an unauthenticated client takes over the account: it can list and delete the victim's notes and reach the authenticated export endpoint. The source has no deployment config, so whether a given deployment leaves the variables unset is outside the repository. The code defect is that provisioning fails open. Sandbox run sbx-00001 shows the exploit behavior under both conditions.

evidence.description: Fallback token 'change-me-a' for alice when ALICE_TOKEN is unset. An empty env value is accepted as-is.
Fallback token 'change-me-b' for bob when BOB_TOKEN is unset.
The only pre-check is the 'Bearer ' prefix. An empty token is not rejected.
Comparison against the possibly default or empty stored token, with no check that the stored token is configured and non-empty.
The test suite authenticates with the default 'change-me-a', which shows the fallback is the effective default credential.

record.intended_behavior: An account whose token is not configured (unset or empty) must be impossible to log into. An empty presented token must always be rejected. No credential value may live in source.

poc_test.expectation: On the current code it exits 1 with AssertionError 'ACCEPTED change-me-a as alice'. After the patch it prints 'ok' and exits 0.

remediation.patch:
--- a/notesapp/storage.py
+++ b/notesapp/storage.py
@@ -2,9 +2,16 @@
 
 EXPORT_DIR = os.environ.get("NOTES_EXPORT_DIR", "/var/lib/notesapp/exports")
 
+
+def _token(var):
+    """Return the configured token, or None (account disabled) if unset/empty."""
+    value = os.environ.get(var, "")
+    return value or None
+
+
 USERS = {
-    "alice": {"id": "alice", "token": os.environ.get("ALICE_TOKEN", "change-me-a")},
-    "bob": {"id": "bob", "token": os.environ.get("BOB_TOKEN", "change-me-b")},
+    "alice": {"id": "alice", "token": _token("ALICE_TOKEN")},
+    "bob": {"id": "bob", "token": _token("BOB_TOKEN")},
 }
 
 NOTES = {
--- a/notesapp/auth.py
+++ b/notesapp/auth.py
@@ -13,8 +13,14 @@
     if not header.startswith("Bearer "):
         raise AuthError("missing token")
     token = header[len("Bearer "):]
+    if not token:
+        raise AuthError("missing token")
+    presented = token.encode("utf-8", "surrogatepass")
     for user in USERS.values():
-        if hmac.compare_digest(user["token"], token):
+        expected = user["token"]
+        if not expected:
+            continue
+        if hmac.compare_digest(expected.encode("utf-8", "surrogatepass"), presented):
             return user
     raise AuthError("invalid token")
 
--- a/tests/test_notes.py
+++ b/tests/test_notes.py
@@ -1,3 +1,7 @@
+import os
+
+os.environ.setdefault("ALICE_TOKEN", "test-token-alice")
+
 from notesapp import notes
 
 
@@ -8,5 +12,5 @@

-    status, body = notes.list_notes(Req("change-me-a"))
+    status, body = notes.list_notes(Req(os.environ["ALICE_TOKEN"]))

remediation.strategy: Remove the hard-coded fallback tokens. Treat an unset or empty token as a disabled account. Reject an empty presented token. Compare bytes so non-ASCII input raises AuthError instead of TypeError. Update the existing test to provision its own token through the environment.

record.root_cause: Credential provisioning fails open. storage.USERS substitutes hard-coded, publicly known tokens when the env vars are missing and keeps empty values. current_user never checks that the expected token is configured and non-empty, or that the presented token is non-empty.

impact.rationale: Full authentication bypass and takeover of the affected accounts. An anonymous client can read and delete every note of each user who has no configured token, and can reach the authenticated export endpoint.

likelihood.rationale: This is the out-of-the-box behaviour. Nothing warns the operator, and the shipped test depends on the default. It still requires that the operator did not set strong values, and the repository has no deployment config to show which way it goes.

threat_model.affected_resource: Every user account (alice, bob): all of their private notes (read via GET /notes) and deletion authority over them (DELETE /notes/<id>), plus the authenticated-only GET /export surface
threat_model.assumption_broken: Bearer tokens are operator-provisioned secrets. The code instead silently uses publicly known fallback tokens when the variables are unset, and accepts an empty token when a variable is set to ''.
threat_model.attacker: Any HTTP client who can reach dispatch() and has read the public source or test fixture
threat_model.starting_capability: Can send arbitrary requests with an Authorization header. Knows the literal strings 'change-me-a' and 'change-me-b' from notesapp/storage.py and tests/test_notes.py.

record.title: Hard-coded fallback bearer tokens and empty-token acceptance let anyone authenticate as any user

trace.description: Any HTTP client's request is routed to a handler, for example notes.list_notes for GET /notes. The dispatcher adds no authentication of its own.
The handler authenticates the caller only through current_user(request).
The token is taken verbatim from the header after 'Bearer '. An empty token is allowed.
The expected token is os.environ.get('ALICE_TOKEN', 'change-me-a'): the hard-coded public default when unset, '' when set empty.
hmac.compare_digest(user['token'], token) matches the public default, or '' against '', and returns the victim user object. The handler then acts as that user.

record.description: get_note authenticates the caller but never checks that the caller owns the requested note. Note ids are small sequential integers, so any authenticated user can enumerate /notes/1, /notes/2, ... and read other users' private title and body. The sibling delete_note enforces require_owner and list_notes filters by owner. get_note is the only note-access path without per-owner isolation. No middleware, decorator or dispatch-level check compensates: dispatch routes straight to the handler.

evidence.description: Returns the note without calling require_owner or comparing note owner to user id
Sibling delete_note calls require_owner, showing the intended control
require_owner exists but get_note does not use it
States users must only see and change their own notes
Note ids are sequential small integers (1, 2), so they are trivially enumerable; storage.get has no owner filter (line 16-17)

record.intended_behavior: GET /notes/<id> returns a note only to its owner. Other users should get the same response as for a nonexistent note (404) or a 403.

poc_test.expectation: On current code bob gets (200, alice's note), so the assertion fails and the script exits non-zero. With the patch bob gets 404 and the script prints 'ok' and exits 0.

remediation.patch:
--- a/notesapp/notes.py
+++ b/notesapp/notes.py
@@ -12,6 +12,6 @@ def list_notes(request):
 def get_note(request, note_id):
     user = current_user(request)
     note = storage.get(int(note_id))
-    if note is None:
+    if note is None or note["owner"] != user["id"]:
         return 404, {"error": "not found"}
     return 200, note
remediation.strategy: Enforce ownership in get_note. Treat a non-owned note the same as a missing one (404) so ids do not become an existence oracle. Alternatively call require_owner, as delete_note does.

record.root_cause: notes.get_note resolves the caller with current_user but drops the result and never calls require_owner (or filters by owner) before returning storage.get(id).

impact.rationale: Full cross-user read of every user's private note content, defeating the documented per-owner isolation

likelihood.rationale: Any authenticated user can exploit it with a single request and guessable sequential ids
